title: Min-Max Scale
statement: Implement `minmax(xs)`, scaling a non-empty list into the unit interval. For each x return (x − min) / (max − min). If max equals min, return a list of zeros of the same length so a constant feature does not divide by zero.

hints: Find min and max in one or two passes.
The original minimum maps to 0 and the maximum maps to 1 when they differ.

approaches.name: Affine map
approaches.explanation: Min-max is an affine map onto 0..1. It is sensitive to outliers, unlike z-scores.

editorial: Min-max scaling sends the smallest training value to 0 and the largest to 1, with linear interpolation between them. Neural nets with saturating activations often train more calmly when features share a scale. Fit min and max on the training fold only, then apply those constants to validation and test rows. A constant feature has no range; returning zeros is the safe, deterministic choice and matches a column of no information.
